Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Female gender; family history of migraines; possible genetic predisposition to migraine; baseline sensitivity to light
- Precipitating factors: New work project; high screen time; environmental triggers (light sensitivity)
- Perpetuating factors: Recurrent headaches with partial relief from NSAIDs; possible suboptimal acute analgesia strategy; ongoing work stress; possible dehydration if fluid intake reduced
- Protective factors: Living with roommates; access to primary care; engaged in seeking medical evaluation; family awareness of migraines
- Summary: Headache presentation consistent with migraine with photophobia and nausea in a patient with relevant family history. MOH considered given NSAID use; tension-type features may also contribute. No red flags documented (no fever, no focal neuro deficits, no progressive AMS). The presentation is largely somatic with an emphasis on pain management and functional impairment at work; no explicit mental health disorder identified at this time, but stress and coping with recurrent pain may influence mood/anxiety.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Headache with suspected migraine; functional impact on work and concentration

Patient Goal(s):
- Achieve meaningful reduction in headache intensity/frequency
- Restore ability to work with comfortable screen use and less photophobia
- Simple, effective acute treatment plan; avoid medication overuse
- Clarity on prognosis and next steps (possible prophylaxis if headaches recur)

Clinical Goal(s):
- Alleviate acute headache pain; improve functionality within 1–2 weeks
- Establish headache diary to identify triggers and patterns
- Optimize analgesia; consider alternative agent if NSAIDs insufficient
- If headaches persist or worsen, pursue further evaluation (neurology/eye exam) and consider prophylactic options

Actions (Patient):
- Maintain a headache diary (onset, duration, intensity, triggers, NSAID use, response to treatment)
- Adhere to prescribed analgesic plan; report inadequate relief or adverse effects
- Schedule and complete an eye examination if visual symptoms persist or worsen
- Implement non-pharmacologic strategies: regular hydration, consistent sleep, stress management, screen-time breaks, light sensitivity management (e.g., sunglasses, dim lighting when symptomatic)
- Monitor for red-flag symptoms (sudden new severe headache, fever, neck stiffness with altered mental status, persistent visual loss, weakness)

Actions (Clinician/GP):
- Provide analgesic plan:
  - Ibuprofen: current use reported; assess dose adequacy; if needed, adjust per safety guidelines (documented in plan: patient reported up to 3 tablets/day; clinician advised up to 2 tablets per dose, up to three times daily)
  - Consider alternative/adjunct acute analgesics: naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript); acetaminophen (paracetamol) or codeine as potential short-term options (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Discuss and initiate a clear plan to avoid MOH: limit NSAID use to recommended maximum and avoid daily use without medical review
- If indicated, prescribe short-term analgesia and/or combination therapy; document dose/route/frequency when prescribed
- Recommend headache diary and review; schedule follow-up in 1–2 weeks
- Consider prophylaxis discussion if headaches become frequent or refractory to acute therapy; plan to reassess in follow-up
- Eye health: encourage repeat eye exam given photophobia and long-standing glasses use; refer for ophthalmology/optometry if symptoms persist
- Provide education on triggers and non-pharmacologic strategies; discuss hydration, sleep regularity, stress management, ergonomic workspace adjustments
- Coordinate care with primary care for monitoring; arrange follow-up

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: migraine vs tension-type headache features, triggers (light sensitivity, stress, screen time), acute treatment options, risks of overuse of NSAIDs, importance of headache diary, when to seek urgent care (new neurological symptoms, fever, confusion, neck stiffness, vision loss)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Headache worsening or new/red flag symptoms (fever, neck stiffness with AMS, focal weakness, slurred speech, severe thunderclap pain, visual loss)
- Coping Strategies: Hydration, consistent sleep schedule, minimize screen glare, regular breaks during work, stress management techniques, limiting analgesic overuse

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (without aura) – Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Unilateral/right-eye predominant pain, photophobia, nausea, gradual daily worsening over 3 days; family history of migraines; prior relief with NSAIDs in past
- Tension-Type Headache – Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Dull, diffuse pain with work-related stress and high screen time; however photophobia and nausea favor migraine over tension-type
- Medication-Overuse Headache (MOH) – Likelihood: Low to Medium
  - Justification: Regular NSAID use (three tablets/day) for a couple of days; potential contributor to persistent symptoms; short-term use limits MOH likelihood but warrants consideration and monitoring
- Meningitis/Encephalitis – Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Neck stiffness and photophobia present; but absence of fever, AMS, and rapid progression lowers probability
- Other broad etiologies (e.g., sinusitis, intracranial pathology) – Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Some symptoms overlap; not strongly supported by current history

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: MSE not recorded; formal risk assessment not performed; explicit diagnoses and follow-up plan partially described but limited details on prognosis and long-term management; exact medication doses for prescribed alternatives not documented in transcript
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: Not observed; plan aligns with migraine/tension-type features described; no explicit psychiatric diagnosis
- Transcript quality notes: Dialogue shows initial presentation focused on headache with light sensitivity and focal eye pain; lacked full neuro exam and vitals in transcript; no documented red-flag neurological signs; missing objective measurements (vision tests, neuro exam) not captured in transcript

End of Mental Health Care Plan
